newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to tighten loan controls on conglomerates.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to tighten loan controls on conglomerates.

text.p: The Bank of Korea said on Thursday it would limit lending by any individual bank to a single industrial group to 45 percent of its net worth from August 1.
Lending caps now apply only to top-10 "chaebol" conglomerates.
The new limits would be imposed on all business groups, a central bank statement said. It added that the current, narrowly imposed limits had allowed second-tier groups to borrow huge sums.
Conglomerates with outstanding loans above the newly-imposed limits would have to repay the money within three years, although the Office of Bank Supervision would have power to approve exceptions.
The new curbs would apply to loans and payment guarantees on won-denominated debt, the statement said.
They were aimed at preventing a bank from being beholden to big borrowers.
It noted that the stricken Hanbo Group had loans and payment guarantees from Korea First Bank equivalent to 93.5 percent of the bank's net worth at the end of 1996.
Hanbo hit trouble after its flagship Hanbo Steel Co was declared insolvent in January after piling up some $5.8 billion in debt.
